## v3.5.0 — 2026-11-07

### Implemented
- **Operator window: workbench pane.** Window 1 now carries a second, tall interactive shell on the far right, beside the board and the command line. Its width is `[dashboard] operator_workbench_pct` (percent of the window, default 40; `0` removes it). When the window is narrower than `operator_workbench_min_cols` (default 160), or a board column would get fewer than 15 columns beside it, the workbench is left out; a client that attaches from a narrower terminal, or a resize, moves it to its own window named `workbench` until the window is wide enough again.
- **Operator window: one AGENTS column.** By default the board shows BUGS, PRIORITIES, REQUIREMENTS and one AGENTS column listing every PM, CODER, WRITER, TESTER and CM task, newest first per project. `[dashboard] operator_board_agents = split` restores the five role columns. The visibility window keeps its eight columns either way.
- **Operator skills.** The repository ships one skill per assistant CLI, staged under `skills/claude/pgai-agent-kanban/` and `skills/codex/pgai-agent-kanban/` in the kanban root. `scripts/install-skills.sh` copies every staged skill into the Claude Code and Codex skill homes; `--list` shows each skill as `new`, `same`, `changed` or `invalid` per provider, `--dry-run` prints the plan, `--force` overwrites a changed copy, `--dir` and `--provider` install your own skills from another directory. Install removes nothing and skips a provider whose CLI is not on `PATH`. `GET /skills` lists the staging directory over REST.
- **Reset keeps unmerged work.** `scripts/reset.sh` on a task whose feature branch holds commits no other ref reaches now keeps the branch and the progress log, prints the tip and commit count, and marks the task to resume from that branch on its next dispatch. `--discard-branch` deletes the branch instead, warning how many commits it drops. `--force` alone never discards a branch. The wake's stale-active sweep keeps an orphaned task's branch the same way instead of force-deleting it.
- **Release hooks are bounded.** Every pre-squash, pre-tag and post-tag hook runs in its own process group under `[release] hook_timeout_seconds` (default 900). Past the limit the whole group, including anything the hook forked, gets SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after 5 seconds, and the hook counts as failed.
- **OVERWATCH verbs are bounded.** The cancel, unwind and release verbs the decision wake runs are limited by `[overwatch] verb_timeout_seconds` (default 3600) in their own process group; a verb that overruns is recorded as failed and the wake continues.
- **Six runtime knobs moved into `kanban.cfg`.** `[discovery] settle_seconds` and `reject_threshold`, `[cleanup] task_retention_days`, `[verify] deep_verify_freshness_window_days`, `[dashboard] status_max_width` and `arm_timeout_seconds`. The matching `PGAI_*` environment variables still win when set.
- **Planner ticket sizing.** Hygiene ride-alongs carried on a bug bundle are grouped by area into tickets of at most four items each, however many tickets that takes, instead of being packed into at most two tickets. A ticket is one agent session with one time budget; small tickets finish, show on the board and verify on their own.
- **Entry scripts work through a symlink.** Every operator script under `scripts/` finds its library directory from the resolved script path, so a symlink to it on your `PATH` runs like the real file.
- **The last-released version survives a missing tag.** When a project's dev tree holds no release tag carrying the project's branch prefix, the resolver answers from `release-state.md`'s `## Last Released` instead of `v0.0.0`. Before, deleting the tag made the board show every finished requirement as unreleased and would have numbered the next bundle from `v0.0.0`.

## v3.0.0 — 2026-10-28

### Implemented
- **Releases ship by default.** The three ship-policy triggers that used to halt a project now ship the release with a status of NON-FUNCTIONAL or KNOWN-BUGS, record an auto-ship event and file a bug. Set `ship_posture = matrix` in `kanban.cfg` or a project's `project.cfg` to restore the halts. A lane that pushes to a remote also needs `ship_posture_confirm_remote = true`, otherwise it keeps the matrix behaviour.
- **Verification that cannot run is retried once, then the release ships anyway.** A blocked or missing tester report requeues verification. If it fails again the release ships NON-FUNCTIONAL and writes an inbox entry. A release run that arrives while the requeued verification is still pending waits for it instead of shipping unverified.
- **Mechanical release failures resolve without a halt.** A squash conflict cancels and rebundles the release candidate and names the conflicting paths in the inbox. A refused push ships locally and records a push-lag event. The push-lag check pushes main and the tag once the remote accepts them, and deletes the leftover release-candidate branch it recorded. A tag already on the remote writes an inbox entry and changes nothing locally. The hook, squash-pollution, fidelity and version gates still halt, and now write their reason to the inbox as well.
- **A blocked task parks only itself.** Independent tasks in the same batch keep running, as do other projects. Only tasks that name the blocked one as a prerequisite wait.
- **Provider errors retry instead of parking.** A run cut short by a transient provider error (rate limit, overload, a safeguard abort) is recorded with its own reason code, matched against one shared signature table, whether the wake saw the error or the agent reported the block itself. The task requeues on a timed ladder up to `[wake] transient_retry_cap` before it reaches the inbox. A blocked planner, tester or release task, which the chain cannot continue without, requeues on a ladder of its own before any inbox entry. Ladder retries do not count as repeats for the runaway detector.
- **OVERWATCH decision wake.** The hourly sweep runs a decision wake for every project. Anything it can resolve with an operator verb, it resolves. Anything that needs a human answer but does not endanger the pipeline goes to the inbox. Runaway detection stops a project when releases, release-candidate cycles, identical blocks or inbox entries exceed configured rates in a window. Design decisions, version changes, provider changes, operator halts and code edits stay human-only.
- **Operator inbox.** One file per project holds the open questions and their answers. `scripts/inbox.sh --project <name> list | answer --id <ID> --answer <text> | close --id <ID>`. The dashboard shows one line per entry and the newest question on the attention pane.
- **Bug convergence.** A bug that needs an operator answer is marked `needs-operator` and excluded from bundling, ship-time promotion and tester re-filing until the inbox entry is answered. Intake refuses a draft that reports the same defect as an open bug and names that bug. A loop detector closes remaining duplicates. Bounded deferral opens a bugfix bundle when deferred bugs grow too many or too old, even while requirements are queued. Ride-along lets the planner attach a capped number of deferred bugs to a requirement release.
- **Per-project test runners.** Each project names its own targeted and pre-merge test commands under `[testing]` in `project.cfg`. The planner writes exactly those commands into ticket acceptance criteria, whatever shape the runner's option list takes. A project with none set gets no runner criteria.
- **Reliability streaks.** One ledger records every block with its class, cause and reason. Each project shows two streaks, hands-off and clean, as releases and hours, on the metrics pane, in `metrics-report.sh --reliability` and over a read-only REST route. `scripts/reliability-backfill.sh` reconstructs the ledger from existing evidence.
- **Task-liveness records.** Every dispatched task leaves a record naming its process, so the kanban can tell a live task from a dead one. Records are removed when the task ends and leftovers are swept by cleanup.
- **Release lifecycle hooks on every project.** The pre-squash, pre-tag and post-tag hook points resolve through a config key, a kanban-side hooks folder, or a file travelling in the repository, in that order. A failing hook now stops the release with an inbox entry rather than a bare halt.
- **Template drift notice.** Install and upgrade report when the project README template changed since a project was seeded and print the diff command.

## v2.41.0 — 2026-10-15

### Implemented
- **"Why isn't it moving?" in one line.** `why.sh` prints one verdict per project (RUNNING, BLOCKED, HALTED, IDLE or STUCK-LOCK) with the cause and a runnable fix. `--details` adds lock holders, queues and posture.
- **A full operator API.** Every operator verb has a REST twin: halt, halt-after, defer, wake-now, intake, cancel and unwind RC, deep-verify, add and remove project, archive. The CLI and the API call the same code. Loopback-only, with a versioned interface contract.
- **Ship by default, with a record.** HALT means "shipping would make things worse", not "the tester found something". Findings ship as known issues and become the next RC's bugs. Each project has a ship posture (`matrix` or `always`); `cm/release.sh --decide-only` previews the decision and `--force --reason` overrides it with a recorded reason.
- **Low-severity bugs wait their turn.** Bugs at or below `deferred_bug_level` do not set the release tempo; they ride along when a more serious bug opens an RC.
- **OVERWATCH clears blocks itself.** Blocked tasks carry a structured block record. OVERWATCH resolves the mechanical cases (timeouts, provider refusals, stale worktrees, merge-only gates) and writes a short diagnosis for the rest.
- **Dashboard v2.** Fourteen fixed windows plus one drill window per registered project: an operator window with a shell, a schedule window with per-agent firings, metrics with time spent blocked, and a human-review window.
- **Containers you can leave running.** `docker/build.sh <flavor>` builds the debian, rocky9 or claude-abliterated image (a custom Claude build for local LLMs). `container-up.sh`, `container-down.sh` (soft stop) and `container-status.sh` run the kanban detached in one named container.
- **Finished work archives itself.** After each release, finished items beyond the newest 55 per category move to `archive/<project>/`, logged and restorable with `archive.sh --restore`.

None

## v2.4.0 — 2026-08-09

v2.4.0 is the fourth public release: the resilient-autonomy era.

### Implemented
- **The Loop doctrine, as canon and census.** The kanban's first
  principles are now written where every agent reads them on every
  wake: the system is a loop — input in, verified output out,
  continuing on new work or on the bugs its own verifier files.
  Bugs are the healing mechanism; blocking is reserved for work
  that moves the system backwards. Every gate, guard, and refusal
  in the shipped tree is inventoried in a blocking-site census and
  classified against the doctrine; a census lint keeps future
  gates honest. Stopping is now a design decision with a paper
  trail, not a side effect.

- **Resilient verification — findings file bugs, not block
  releases.** The gated runners distinguish breakage (syntax,
  compile, import — still fatal) from quality findings (every
  lint — printed, recorded in a machine-readable findings file,
  and carried into the TESTER report, which cites or files the
  bug). The ship-policy matrix maps green-suites-with-findings to
  ship-with-concerns. The completion gate keeps its delivery
  checks — work merged, worktree clean — and nothing else.

- **Dual-channel errors everywhere.** Every refusal, HALT, and
  fail-loud site speaks two channels: a stable machine key for
  tooling, and a plain-language message with a runnable remedy for
  a stranger with no ledger open. error / message / remedy — the
  errno/strerror contract, for the agent age.

- **Autonomous block resolution.** OVERWATCH gained a resolution
  stage: blocked tasks are triaged against a prescription matrix
  and unblocked autonomously where the fix is mechanical, with
  scope ceilings, per-project locks, full narration, and a
  configuration kill-switch. Blocks that once waited for an
  operator now heal between wakes.

- **The REST control plane and the browser operator surface.** A
  loopback-only FastAPI service (versioned ICD, now 1.3.0) exposes
  the operator verbs — queues, tasks, intake, reset, HALT state —
  with an API-parity lint holding CLI and API to the same surface;
  a browser UI renders the board read-write for operators who
  prefer glass to tmux. Local-observation-only remains law.

- **Pluggable workflow types.** Release, document, and
  testing-only workflows are plugins under team/workflows/ — a
  manifest of capability flags and hook functions per type; the
  engine queries capabilities and never branches on a type name.
  Operators can author new workflow types without touching engine
  code.

- **Version-targeted, state-safe deployment.** install.sh lays
  down any tagged version; upgrade.sh targets any tag forward of
  the current install — forward-only by semver, because upgrades
  preserve state and state must never be newer than code. VERSION
  is a committed, self-identifying file written at ship time.
  Fresh installs may choose any version; that is the sanctioned
  path backwards.

- **Release-engine hardening from production fire.** The release
  ceremony now checks out the RC before running hooks (releases no
  longer require a parked dev tree); HALTs raised by a project's
  release freeze that project only; stale per-task worktrees are
  detected and removed at reset and before branch deletion; the
  completion gate accepts merge evidence from branch history when
  a feature branch was already tidied away. Each fix carries a
  fixture reproducing the production transcript that taught it.

- **Content-described notes.** Release notes and shipped
  documentation describe what changed in plain language — the
  behavior fixed, the contract added — never by internal ticket
  number. The notes you are reading were generated under that
  rule, and a provenance lint (a quality finding, per the
  doctrine) keeps it true.

### Fixed
None

## v1.27.0 — 2026-07-26

v1.27.0 is the third public release: the container-and-credibility era.

### Implemented
- **Containerized deployment — the workspace model.** Debian and
  Rocky Linux 9 image flavors with a fully audited dependency set;
  a minimal fail-loud entrypoint that lands an interactive shell at
  the kanban root; a launcher (`scripts/container-shell.sh`) with a
  config-selectable engine — docker or podman. The container is a
  workspace: the operator starts the scheduler and the dashboard
  exactly as on a host. `docs/docker.md` is rewritten to match and
  held to the executable-documentation standard.
- **Relocatable scheduling.** Pseudocron configs carry
  root-relative commands and run from the resolved kanban root —
  the same config works on a host, in a container, or anywhere the
  install moves.
- **Coding standards, self-enforced.** `docs/coding-standards.md`
  binds every code-producing agent, backed by a lint fleet
  (help-presence, comment-provenance, import-completeness) that the
  framework runs against its own tree — and has already used to
  reject its own work.
- **Executable documentation.** A doc-lint harness runs every
  fenced command in the public docs verbatim; links, fossils, and
  feature coverage are gated the same way.
- **Committed VERSION.** Releases stamp their identity into the
  tree at ship time; installs and containers report exactly what
  they run.
- **Dashboards observe locally.** No dashboard window performs
  network git operations — render paths read the local tree only,
  missing state degrades with a clear on-screen message, and a
  lint gate plus a network-stub fixture keep it that way. Displays
  can no longer contend with releases for the repository lock or
  wedge on fresh SSH state.
- **Operator experience.** An operator dashboard window — the full
  board over a working shell, the container operator's workspace;
  configurable status glyphs; force-reset with worktree cleanup; a
  provider extended-thinking compatibility toggle for
  proxy-restricted deployments; complete in-container test
  tooling.

### Fixed
Consolidated across the arc, described by pattern:
- **Control-plane hardening from an external code audit**, fixed and regression-tested by the framework itself: the safety observer resolves the same per-project lock the agents hold and can never remove an operator-placed HALT; transient-error retries live in one durable machine-readable record with one owner and one ceiling; task dispatch honors the assigned agent and fails closed on invalid roles — on both provider lanes; task-level model overrides take precedence over environment configuration, as documented.
- **Release-engineering semantics.** Cancelled version numbers free cleanly for re-use, bug fixes always precede feature work at selection, and the cancel/reset recovery drill is race-guarded — production lessons, encoded as fixtures.
- **Verification honesty.** The post-suite listener-cleanliness gate attributes leaked servers to the run that spawned them, so stale cross-task orphans no longer fail unrelated verifications; documentation commands are annotated and executed by the harness rather than trusted.
The public Known Issue disclosed at v1.23.0 is resolved as of this
release:
- KI-1.23.0.1 — resolved (testing-only intake items are closed by the machinery: completion event hook plus a sweep census)

### Known Issues
None

## v1.23.0 — 2026-07-14

v1.23.0 is the second public release and the consolidation of everything since v1.0.0: the pluggable workflow architecture, the operator REST API with its browser dashboard, the OVERWATCH observer and PO intake agent, a unified fail-loud environment contract across every entry point, and a third shipped workflow type — testing-only — certified end-to-end with zero operator interventions.

### Implemented
- **Pluggable workflow types.** Workflows are now plugins: a
  directory with a manifest and eight hooks. The engine queries
  capabilities (version semantics, git mode, roster, finalize), never
  type names, and fails closed on unknown types. A generator
  scaffolds new types; `validate-workflow.sh` gates them; a
  ready-status flip is the human gate. `release` and `document` are
  themselves plugins; custom types survive upgrades by contract.
- **testing-only — the third workflow type.** Audits something
  already shipped: a read-only, detached-worktree verification of any
  project's tag. Label versioning (nothing consumed), a pm+tester
  roster, a report as the finalize product, and machinery closure of
  the intake item. Genuine findings are filed on the target project's
  own lane with full provenance. Certified end-to-end — selection to
  report to closure — with zero operator interventions, during which
  it found and filed real defects in the project it was auditing.
- **Operator REST API + browser dashboard.** Seventeen operations
  behind a loopback FastAPI service with Swagger docs, universal
  `dry_run` support and a `warnings` field on every response,
  strict-validation 422s proven to fire before any subprocess, and a
  structured read layer (board, project metadata, metrics/costs as
  JSON, log access with server-side path confinement, trace
  index/fetch). API parity with the CLI is lint-enforced: a script
  growing a flag fails the suite until the API matches. The browser
  dashboard covers board, attention, inspector, metrics, logs, and a
  gated operate surface. Both ship labeled experimental.
- **OVERWATCH + PO.** OVERWATCH runs an hourly zero-token health
  sweep and a daily LLM deep-clean, and wakes immediately when any
  agent blocks (storm-collapsed, self-trigger-guarded, HALT-gated).
  PO turns a plain-language brief into a formal requirements doc
  under a nine-rule authoring method with an explicit assumptions
  ledger.
- **Fail-loud environment contract.** Every script — shell and
  Python — establishes its environment through one bootstrap:
  self-locate, source the install's `shell-env`, fail loudly with the
  exact path if the root is still unset. Explicit operator exports
  always win. Enforced by lint on both runtimes in every gated run.
- **Provider abstraction hardened.** One config line switches
  providers; per-role model overrides; the resolved model is
  wake-stamped into each task's status as an execution record.
- **Release engine resilience.** The release step is resumable at
  its checkpoint boundaries after interruption or damage;
  cancellation drills are part of the standing verification; the
  CHANGELOG and ICD freshness gates hold byte-exactness on the
  released line while tolerating exactly the legitimate in-flight-RC
  shapes.
- **Two-repo law.** Live installs import only from themselves and
  fail loudly on their own brokenness; repository checkouts are data,
  never a runtime dependency. Codified in the SOP, enforced in the
  dashboard's import paths, and testable in one move: flipping any
  dev tree's branch changes nothing about live behavior.

### Fixed
Consolidated across the arc: plugin-era capability fixes through the
entire engine (registration, eligibility, filename handling, version
ceilings, task-state transitions, graph materialization, folder
recycling), API lifecycle and contract hardening, dashboard
truncation and import-path integrity, release-gate tolerance
corrections, and operator-tool recipes brought current with the
selection model. Defects are tracked on the internal ledger and
described by pattern in the CHANGELOG.
All five public Known Issues disclosed at v1.0.0 are resolved as of
this release:
- KI-1.0.0.1 — resolved
- KI-1.0.0.2 — resolved
- KI-1.0.0.3 — resolved
- KI-1.0.0.4 — resolved
- KI-1.0.0.5 — resolved
